description: ReEDS, the Regional Energy Deployment System, is a capacity planning and dispatch model for the electricity system of the United States and the flagship long-term power sector model of the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR, formerly the National Renewable Energy Laboratory). It has served as the primary analytic tool for many NLR studies of electricity sector questions, and example results are published in the laboratory's Scenario Viewer. The model represents the U.S. electricity system over the long term. The source code, written in Python, GAMS and Julia, is available at no cost on GitHub under the BSD 3-Clause licence, with dated stable releases (latest tag 2026.09.08), documentation on GitHub Pages and training videos on the NLR Learning YouTube channel; the citation file lists Patrick Brown and colleagues for ReEDS 2.0. Caveats: while Python and Julia are free, GAMS requires a commercial licence from its vendor, and the model is designed for the U.S. electricity system, not as a generic framework. Simulation uses are capacity planning and optimisation of long-term power sector scenarios. Related records: it compares with model-genx and model-switch and can be explored alongside the Sienna production cost tools in platform-sienna from the same laboratory.
